outcome: Install a repository-wide audit, repair and re-audit system that prevents premature stopping on known authorized work.
authorizedScope: Implement the explicitly requested workflow system, persistence, tests and supported runtime configuration. Preserve Akinza as unfinished work in its own record; do not grant art approval or bypass hook trust.

criteria.expectation: New sessions inherit audit and follow-through requirements tied to the original outcome.
criteria.assessment: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and species workflow require direct inspection, findings, repairs and re-audit; stop boundaries and scope limits are explicit.

criteria.expectation: Mechanism rejects stale reviews and unfinished work, preserves findings and user control, and has meaningful regression coverage.
criteria.assessment: 25 tests pass, including actual Windows hook wrapper. Independent audits found defects that were repaired and covered before stopping. Script cannot prove subjective quality; this limit is documented.

criteria.expectation: Current Akinza audit becomes executable unfinished work, not an approval request or completed milestone.
criteria.assessment: 20 failed criteria and 20 open findings are bound to actual current evidence. Running the checker returns CONTINUE. No model corrections are claimed.

criteria.expectation: Automatic runtime dispatch is verified after the user trusts the exact hook definition.
criteria.assessment: Initial trust was verified. A live ephemeral test exposed Windows nested-shell expansion and exited without enforcement. Corrected the command and passed tests through both Windows shells. Updated definitions are marked modified and require renewed trust before a live retry.

findings.observation: Old passing audits could be reused across chats or later stops.
findings.resolution: Fresh session/request binding and one-use consumption, with new-prompt invalidation.

findings.observation: Interrupt and explicit-stop behavior conflicted with persistence.
findings.resolution: Interrupt takes precedence until new input; user_stop bypasses history without erasing obligations.

findings.observation: Approval and blocker records lacked meaningful stopping boundaries.
findings.resolution: Require existing approval authority and specific decision; blockers cover all remaining nonpassing criteria and no runnable findings.

findings.observation: Findings could disappear and invalid closures could advance history.
findings.resolution: Canonical persistent inventory retains newly observed obligations on failed checks; per-finding failure baselines and actual-byte validation precede resolution.

findings.observation: Codex requires exact-definition hook trust before non-managed hooks execute.

blocker.externalDependency: User review/trust of repository hooks in Codex; actual dispatch confirmation
blocker.attempts: Verified saved user trust, then observed real lifecycle handler failures. Reproduced nested PowerShell expansion, fixed the Windows command, and passed all 25 regression tests with PowerShell/cmd event coverage. Installed corrected definition and confirmed modified trust status. Awaiting renewed user trust for live retry; no bypass used.
blocker.unblocksWhen: User reviews/trusts this hooks.json definition on a supported Codex surface and a real lifecycle dispatch is observed.

audit.comparison: Observed actual live dispatch after user trust. Failure evidence led to a Windows command repair and broader shell-boundary regression coverage. Independent reviewer approved the correction; a minor event-specific test gap was also closed. Successful automatic enforcement is still pending a trusted live retry.
audit.regressions: Verified explicit stops, interrupts, per-chat isolation, changed evidence, retained findings and blocked approval. Unrelated validator drafts remain untouched.
audit.scopeCheck: This is the explicit workflow-system request. It does not complete or erase the ongoing creature task, promise aesthetic judgment from hashes, or alter global app trust.
